chapter: Dreamland and the Tuxedo dance hall
title: What Lincoln Park looked like
summary: The interviewer asks about Lincoln Park; Manetta describes a fenced open lot with a whitewashed bandstand and baseball games.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Easter Monday morning. I wanted to ask one, just a couple little questions, but was Lincoln, Lincoln Gardens just like a big field, or did it have a fence around it so they could charge admission and so on? Or was it just a big...

Lincoln Park. Lincoln Park. Oh, Lincoln Park was a big... Just like a big oak? A big oakland park. Mm-hmm. Was there a wall around it? Huh? Was there a wall or fence around it? Oh, sure. It was surrounded by a tape of a big square. High feather board planks. Mm-hmm. Inside, a fine big bandstand. Was it colorful? I mean, was it painted, or... Oh, yeah. It was whitewashed. Whitewashed.
Is there anything like a carnival to have merry-go-rounds or ferris wheel, anything like that? No. No, no, no, no. Nothing like that? Not like Coney Island.
They'd have it. They'd use it to read it out for like baseballs, playing, and things like that.
